metadata.title: e-kariyerim
metadata.description: Track your job applications in one place.

hero.title: You applied. So what happened next?
hero.subtitle: Track your job applications in one place. See what stage each one is at, how long you've been waiting, and which applications got a response.

problem.title: Applying is easy. Keeping track isn't.
problem.body1: You apply to a few listings. Then a few more. A few weeks later, it's dozens of applications.
problem.body2: It gets hard to remember which company you applied to, when, who responded, what stage you're at, and which ones quietly disappeared.
problem.outcome: Dozens of applications. Different statuses. Different dates.
problem.question: What happened to this one again?

afterApply.title: The real story starts after you apply.
afterApply.note: Not every application follows the same path — e-kariyerim makes it visible what stage you're at, and how long you've been waiting.

features.title: What e-kariyerim does
features.trackingBody: Track company, position, date, source, and status on a single screen.
features.timelineTitle: Know how long you've been waiting
features.timelineBody: See how much time has passed since you applied. Get a reminder when it's time to follow up.
features.analyticsBody: See your own process through metrics like response rate, interview rate, offer rate, and response time.
features.noResponseTitle: Never forget the ones left hanging
features.noResponseBody: Spot applications with no movement in a long time, and easily find the ones that need a follow-up.

linkedinImport.title: Applied to hundreds of jobs? Don't enter them one by one.
linkedinImport.subtitle: Upload your LinkedIn application history. e-kariyerim organizes your applications, cleans up duplicates, and takes you straight to your dashboard.

analytics.title: What can you learn from your applications?
analytics.subtitle: See your response rate, interview rate, and response times in your personal analytics dashboard.

vision.title: We're building something bigger.
vision.body1: Today, you're tracking your own applications.
vision.body2: Tomorrow, anonymous and aggregate candidate data could help everyone understand how hiring processes actually work.
vision.disclaimer: This is a long-term vision that doesn't exist yet. When it does, it will work without targeting individual companies, with a minimum sample size, and on fully anonymous/aggregate data.

mission.statement: A candidate's time is valuable too.
mission.narrative1: They prepared a CV. Researched the company. Applied.
mission.narrative2: Maybe solved a technical test. Maybe sat through an interview.
mission.narrative3: Then waited. A day. A week. Two weeks.
mission.closing: We don't want that to be normal.
mission.closingNote: Even a no is worth more than silence.
mission.philosophy2: Candidates have a right to a response.
mission.philosophy3: A rejection is worth more than silence.
mission.philosophy4: Transparency benefits candidates and companies alike.
mission.philosophy5: Data should be used to improve the system, not to blame people.

dataCollection.title: What data we collect and why
dataCollection.intro: e-kariyerim is a personal tool that helps you track your job applications. To provide the service, we process the following data:
dataCollection.item1: Account information: first name, last name, email address, password (stored hashed).
dataCollection.item2: Application data you enter or import: company, job listing, application status, dates, and notes.
dataCollection.item3: Reminders derived from this data (follow-up suggestions, no-response alerts).
dataCollection.item4: If you turn on Gmail Scanning (an opt-in browser-extension feature), the subject line and a short snippet of a detected status-update email — used to detect a status change and, for a job not yet tracked, to read off the company/role — are stored on your account and, for that detection, sent to OpenAI. This content is first evaluated locally in your browser; only a message that looks job-application-related ever reaches us. See "Cross-border data transfer" below.
dataCollection.outro: This data is used solely to provide you with application tracking and personal analytics features.

crossBorderTransfer.title: Cross-border data transfer
crossBorderTransfer.intro: If you turn on Gmail Scanning, the subject line and a short snippet of each detected status-update email is sent abroad to determine what it means for your application.
crossBorderTransfer.recipient: Recipient: OpenAI, L.L.C. (United States) — our API provider.
crossBorderTransfer.purpose: Purpose: to classify the email's application-status signal, and — for a job not yet tracked — to read off a company name and job title; this only runs when a simpler, local rule-based check doesn't already recognize the email.
crossBorderTransfer.legalBasis: Legal basis: this only happens for Gmail Scanning you turn on yourself in the browser extension; nothing is sent unless you use this feature.
crossBorderTransfer.withdraw: Withdrawal: turn off Gmail Scanning in the browser extension's Settings page. Or delete your account, to stop this entirely.
crossBorderTransfer.sensitiveDataNote: The subject and snippet are also stored on your account (visible to you when reviewing a suggestion) — never the full email body.

retention.title: Retention period
retention.body: Your data is kept until you delete your account. No automatic time-based deletion is applied.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.before: You can export a copy of your data or permanently delete your account at any time. You can do this from the
rights.after: page. Deleting your account permanently removes all application, import, and reminder data tied to your account.

notApplicable.title: Not currently applicable
notApplicable.body: e-kariyerim does not yet offer public/company-wide analytics features. As a result, anonymization/minimum-sample-size controls are not currently applicable — this policy will be updated when these features are added.

overview.title: How e-kariyerim works
overview.intro: e-kariyerim brings your whole job-application process into one place: note down jobs you're interested in without losing track of them, follow the ones you've applied to and their status, get automatic status suggestions from your own emails, and see the whole process summarized on your dashboard. This page walks through everything from creating your account to logging an application with one click from the Chrome extension.

step1.title: Create your account
step1.body: Sign up with your email and password in a few seconds.

step2.title: Track jobs you're interested in
step2.body: Add jobs you haven't applied to yet, but don't want to lose, to Tracked Jobs.

step3.title: Apply and log it
step3.body: Enter it by hand, import your LinkedIn history, or add it with one click from the Chrome extension.

step4.title: Keep the status current
step4.body: Change the status yourself, or turn on Gmail Scanning in the browser extension to get automatic suggestions.

step5.title: See your progress on the dashboard
step5.body: Track your response rate, average response time, and status breakdown at a glance.

gettingStarted.title: Signing Up and Logging In
gettingStarted.intro: Getting started with e-kariyerim only takes a few details — no credit card, no waiting on a confirmation email.

step1.title: Enter your first and last name
step1.body: Used to identify you throughout the app (e.g. the name shown on the dashboard and in the NavBar).

step3.title: Accept the Privacy Policy
step3.body: The account can't be created without checking the consent box under the sign-up form.

step4.title: Submit
step4.body: You're taken straight to the Dashboard — no email verification to wait for.

login.title: Log in
login.body: Log in with the email and password you registered with. On login, your last saved theme (light/dark) and language preference are applied automatically.

calloutTheme.title: Your dark-mode preference carries over at sign-up
calloutTheme.body: If you switched to dark mode in your browser before signing up, your new account opens in dark mode too — new accounts otherwise start in light mode.

dashboard.title: What's on the Dashboard?
dashboard.intro: The Dashboard you land on after logging in summarizes your whole application process on one screen. The "New Application" button in the top right lets you add a new application directly.

tiles.title: Stat tiles
tiles.body: Tiles showing raw numbers, like your total application count and breakdown by status.

analytics.title: Personal Analytics
analytics.body: Tiles showing percentages like response rate and interview rate — how many of your applications get a reply.

responseTime.title: Response Time
responseTime.body: The average and median number of days from applying to first response. If there isn't enough data yet, an empty state is shown instead.

statusChart.title: Status Distribution Chart
statusChart.body: A bar chart of how many applications are in each status (Applied, Interview, Offer, Rejected, ...) — so you can see where things tend to stall.

trackedJobs.title: Note jobs you haven't applied to yet
trackedJobs.intro: Tracked Jobs is a lightweight watchlist for jobs you're interested in but haven't applied to yet. Unlike an Application, it has no status, timeline, or employment type — just company, title, location, job URL, and your notes.

step2.title: Enter the company name and job title
step2.body: Optionally add the location, job URL, and your own notes.

step3.title: Save it
step3.body: The job appears in your list with the date it was added.

step1.title: Click "Mark as Applied" next to the job
step1.body: This opens a small inline form.

step2.title: Enter the employment type and applied date
step2.body: You can add extra notes too.

step3.title: Confirm
step3.body: The job is removed from your tracked list and created as a real Application — you're taken straight to its detail page.

remove.title: Remove a job
remove.body: If you're no longer interested, "Remove" deletes it from the list permanently.

calloutNoEdit.title: There's no direct edit
calloutNoEdit.body: There's currently no way to edit a tracked job's details. If something's wrong, remove it and re-add it; if you've already applied, converting it with "Mark as Applied" and then editing the resulting Application is the way to fix the details.

applications.title: Create, track, edit, and delete your applications
applications.intro: Applications are the heart of e-kariyerim: each one has its own status, timeline, and (if available) job description.

step1.title: Click "New Application" from the Dashboard or Applications page

step2.title: Start typing the company name
step2.body: Companies you've added before are suggested as autocomplete; for a new company, just type it as-is.

step3.title: Enter the job title, job URL, location, and employment type
step3.body: The applied date defaults to today, but you can change it.

step4.title: Optionally add a source and notes, then save
step4.body: The source field can only be chosen when creating — it can't be changed later.

list.title: List, search, filter
list.body: The Applications list is paginated (10 per page) and supports searching by company/title, filtering by status, and sorting by date/company/title/status — all your filters are reflected in the URL, so you can share or bookmark a view.

detail.title: Application detail
detail.body: Opening an application shows its status badge, location, employment type, applied date, job URL (if any) and notes, an event Timeline, and (if available) the job description. Applications created automatically via Gmail Scanning show a "Created from Email" badge.

edit.title: Editing
edit.body: "Edit" on the detail page lets you update the job title, job URL, location, employment type, applied date, and notes. The company name and source can't be changed after creation.

delete.title: Deleting
delete.body: Clicking "Delete" on the detail page opens a confirmation dialog — nothing is deleted until you confirm.

calloutConfirm.title: Deletion can't be undone
calloutConfirm.body: Deleting an application permanently removes its entire history, including its timeline.

step1.title: Click "Change Status" on the detail page

step2.title: Pick the new status from the list
step2.body: Your current status doesn't appear in the list — only the statuses you can move to.

step3.title: Optionally add a note and confirm
step3.body: The change is recorded on the timeline as "Old Status → New Status", along with your note.

statuses.title: What do the statuses mean?
statuses.body: An application can be in one of these statuses: Applied, Screening, Interview, TechnicalInterview, FinalInterview, Offer, Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, Ghosted.

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.body: Below every application is a chronological list of everything that happened to it: creation, submission, recruiter contact, screening, interview scheduled/completed, offer received, follow-up sent, and every status change. It's a quick way to remember an application's history at a glance.

suggestions.title: Automatic status suggestions from your emails
suggestions.intro: Once you turn on Gmail Scanning in the browser extension (see the Chrome Extension page), the system reads status-update emails you open and offers status suggestions — so you don't have to process every update by hand.

how.title: How a suggestion appears
how.body: Once a scanned email is processed, a card appears on the Suggestions page with the company, job title, received date, a confidence percentage, and a suggested status (if any). A suggestion that doesn't match a known application yet is marked with a "New Job" badge; if no clear status could be inferred, the card shows "Still Pending" instead.

step1.title: Review the card
step1.body: Check the subject line and email snippet to make sure the suggestion is about the right application.

step2.title: "Confirm" to apply it, or "Dismiss" to skip it
step2.body: Confirm creates a new application (if it's new) or moves an existing one to the suggested status. Dismiss closes the suggestion without changing anything.

calloutConfidence.title: Check the confidence percentage
calloutConfidence.body: When confidence is low, read the email snippet first — automatic extraction isn't always exact, so you have the final say.

import.title: Bring in your LinkedIn history in bulk
import.intro: Right now the only import method is LinkedIn's own data export file (a .zip). There's no separate CSV uploader.

step1.title: Request your data export from LinkedIn
step1.body: From your LinkedIn account settings, use "Get a copy of your data" to download your export; LinkedIn can take a while to prepare it.

step2.title: Open the Import page in e-kariyerim
step2.body: Go to "Import" from the top navigation.

step3.title: Select and upload the .zip file you downloaded
step3.body: As soon as it uploads, the status switches to "processing".

step4.title: Watch the progress live
step4.body: You'll see a progress bar with the number of rows processed so far; no need to leave the page.

step5.title: Review the summary
step5.body: When it finishes, you'll see how many new applications were added, how many were already there (duplicates), and how many rows couldn't be processed (invalid); any failing rows are listed individually.

calloutCsv.title: Only LinkedIn import is available
calloutCsv.body: There's currently no interface for uploading a hand-prepared CSV file. Applications created through import default to "FullTime" employment type, since LinkedIn's data doesn't specify one — edit the application afterwards if you need to change it.

settings.title: Account Settings
settings.intro: From Settings you can export your data, generate an access token for the Chrome extension, and delete your account. Theme and language are changed from the switchers in the top navigation, not from Settings.

export.title: Export My Data
export.body: Download all of your application, import, and reminder data as a single JSON file.

extension.title: Access token for the Chrome Extension

step2.title: Name the token and click "Generate Token"
step2.body: For example, "Chrome Extension" or the name of the computer you're using.

step3.title: Copy the token right away
step3.body: The value starting with aa_pat_ is shown only once — if you navigate away, you won't see it again.

step4.title: Paste it into the extension's settings
step4.body: See the Chrome Extension section. You can have at most 10 active tokens at a time; revoke one you no longer use with "Revoke" when you need room for a new one.

calloutToken.title: This token grants full access to your account
calloutToken.body: An access token gives full account access, exactly as if you'd logged in with your email and password. Only paste it into your own browser extension install, never share it — if you suspect it's been exposed, revoke it immediately.

delete.title: Delete My Account
delete.body: Enter your password and type "DELETE" into the box to permanently delete your account and all of your data.

calloutIrreversible.title: This can't be undone
calloutIrreversible.body: Once your account is deleted, all of your application, import, and reminder data is permanently gone — there's no way to reverse it.

chromeExtension.title: One-click application logging on LinkedIn and kariyer.net
chromeExtension.intro: The e-kariyerim Chrome extension turns a LinkedIn or kariyer.net job posting into a tracked application with one click — just press "I Applied".

install.title: Installation
install.storeIntro: The e-kariyerim extension is live on the Chrome Web Store — one-click install, no developer mode needed.

step1.title: Generate an access token in Settings
step1.body: See the "Access token for the Chrome Extension" steps in the Settings section.

step2.title: Add the extension to Chrome from the link above
step2.body: Click "Add to Chrome" on the Chrome Web Store page. The extension icon appears in your toolbar.

installManual.title: Alternative: unpacked install (developer/testing only)
installManual.intro: If you can't use the Store version — for example, you're testing an unreleased development build — you can also load the extension manually:

step1.title: Open chrome://extensions
step1.body: Just type it into the address bar and press Enter.

step2.title: Turn on "Developer mode"
step2.body: Found in the top right of the page.

step3.title: Click "Load unpacked" and select the extension folder
step3.body: The extension icon appears in your toolbar.

step1.title: Click the e-kariyerim icon in the toolbar

step2.title: Click "Open Settings" if no token is set yet
step2.body: You can also right-click the icon and choose "Options".

step3.title: Enter the API base URL and your access token, then save
step3.body: Make sure the API URL is correct if you're pointing it at a real deployment.

step1.title: Open a LinkedIn or kariyer.net job posting page

step2.title: Click the extension icon
step2.body: It tries to auto-fill the company, title, and location from the page.

step3.title: Check the fields and correct anything that's off
step3.body: Auto-fill isn't always perfect — every field is editable before you submit.

step4.title: Click "I Applied"
step4.body: Your application is saved to e-kariyerim.

calloutScraping.title: Auto-fill is best-effort
calloutScraping.body: LinkedIn and kariyer.net occasionally change their page layout, which can leave some fields empty. That shows up as a blank field for you to fill in by hand, rather than submitting wrong data.

calloutDedupe.title: Clicking the same job again is safe
calloutDedupe.body: If you click "I Applied" again on the same job posting, it won't create a duplicate — the system finds your existing application by the job's URL and returns that instead.

q1.question: What happens if someone gets hold of my Chrome extension token?
q1.answer: That token grants full access to your account. If you suspect it's been exposed, go to Settings → Browser Extension and "Revoke" it immediately, then generate a new one.

q2.question: Can I get my data back after deleting my account?
q2.answer: No. Account deletion can't be undone; all of your application, import, and reminder data is permanently deleted.

q3.question: What if the Chrome extension reads a job's details wrong?
q3.answer: Nothing gets submitted automatically — every field is editable before you click "I Applied", the popup just gives you a starting point.

q4.question: Does Gmail Scanning read my whole inbox?
q4.answer: No. It's off by default, and once turned on it only reads an email you personally open in Gmail — never your inbox list, never a message you didn't open. The check runs on your device; only a short summary of an email that looks job-application-related is ever sent to e-kariyerim.

q5.question: Can I import a file other than my LinkedIn export (e.g. Excel/CSV)?
q5.answer: Not currently — the only import path is LinkedIn's own data export .zip file.

q6.question: Can I edit a job I'm tracking?
q6.answer: There's no direct edit for Tracked Jobs; if the details are wrong, remove it and re-add it, or if you've already applied, convert it with "Mark as Applied" and update the details on the Application edit page.

q7.question: How many Chrome extension tokens can I have?
q7.answer: Up to 10 active tokens at once. You'll need to revoke one you're not using before generating a new one.

q8.question: Why does employment type always show "Full-Time" on imported or extension-added applications?
q8.answer: Neither LinkedIn's export nor the job pages the extension reads specify an employment type, so it defaults to "FullTime" — edit the application afterwards if you need the correct type.
